Subject: Incident 2026-05-08 — kv-cache eviction spike: postmortem + action items

Hi Hannah,

Summary (short): between 02:42 and 03:10 UTC on 2026-05-08 we observed a sudden cache eviction cascade in the kv-cache layer that caused 10–15s tail latencies for hosted inference requests in us-west-2 for ~28 minutes. Root cause is a rare interaction between the recent prefix-caching change and a load spike that evicted critical KV segments (see timeline).

Impact: ~2.4% of requests experienced latency >5s, ~0.6% errored with 503s while fallback routing warmed. No customer data exposure. Brightbox Health reported elevated tail latencies; we proactively engaged their SRE.

Timeline (high level):
- 02:40 UTC: small traffic surge from Brightbox long-polling test
- 02:42 UTC: cache eviction rate increases sharply; error budget guards trigger fallback to model-variant B
- 03:08 UTC: emergency cache policy rollback applied: evictions limited + forced warming
- 03:10 UTC: latency returns to baseline; monitoring alerts cleared by 03:20 UTC

Root cause: a bug in the eviction heuristic with certain overlapping prefix keys that under extreme access patterns caused cascading evictions. The prefix-caching change reduced memory headroom for cold-population keys and made eviction decisions correlated rather than independent.

Remediations completed in incident window:
1) immediate rollback of the prefix-caching tweak to revert to previous eviction thresholds (Rishi)
2) applied a short-term forced-warm path for the most frequently-accessed keys (SRE runbook)
3) increased monitoring granularity and added a dedicated alert for correlated-eviction patterns (alerts triggered correctly)

Action items (owners + ETA):
- A1: Fix eviction heuristic to consider independent scoring (owner: rishi_malhotra, ETA: 2026-05-18)
- A2: Add integration test to reproduce correlated eviction (owner: vivek_kulkarni, ETA: 2026-05-14)
- A3: Postmortem doc + exec summary for QBR (owner: hannah_schmitt, ETA: 2026-05-09)
- A4: Customer communication template + credit recommendation (owner: laura_bennett / aditya_rao, ETA: 2026-05-10)

Attachments: postmortem PDF + CSV of action items attached.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3CkV-postmortem (postmortem draft + logs)

TL;DR: mitigated quickly, engineering fix in progress, recommend including a one-slide summary in QBR that ties the fix to OKR-Reliability-2 (reduce tail latency).

Happy to discuss — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

Thanks — Hannah
